subject: Post-call: inference fit, SLO priorities & deployment sketch
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice@remotescale.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-09T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: inference fit, SLO priorities & deployment sketch

Hi Alice — thanks again for the time today. Below is a concise recap of what we heard on the call, a pragmatic topology sketch we recommend for validation, and proposed next steps. Attaching the slide deck and a short CSV with sample P95/P99 traces you asked about.

What we heard (pain / constraints)
- Tail latency spikes (P99) during peak batch index jobs are causing timeouts in your pipeline and increased retries.
- Cost volatility: episodic background batch/ETL traffic causes token-cost spikes that impact margin.
- Cold-start KV cache misses for repeated prompts (prefix-heavy workloads).
- Data residency & compliance: SOC2 + VPC isolation are gating procurement; pen test coming from your security team.
- Requirement to pin model versions for deterministic behaviour, plus support for a quantized variant to reduce unit cost.

Business goals (prioritized)
1) User-facing latency: P95 <= 150ms for short responses (<128 tokens), P99 <= 400ms for long responses (>512 tokens).
2) Throughput: steady-state 500 qps with burst capacity to 2k for peak windows.
3) Cost: reduce per-token inference cost by >= 40% vs current hosted baseline (target via batching + 4-bit quantization).
4) Compliance: VPC deployment + SOC2 evidence within procurement timeline (target: 6 weeks).

Technical summary / model requirements
- Model family: customer prefers instruction-tuned ~70B family. Must support KV caching and attention optimizer paths.
- Quantization: need validated 4-bit (QLoRA-style) or int8 path for cost-optimized fallback. Must preserve instruction-following quality.
- Sequence lengths: mixed workload — 85% <256 tokens, 15% up to 2048; plan for dynamic allocation to avoid overprovisioning.
- Determinism: pin model version and tokenizer commit; store model checksum in deployment manifest.

Suggested deployment topology (high level)
- Primary: us-west (multi-GPU pool, reserved capacity for steady 500 qps).
- Secondary: eu-west (warm standby for region failover and residency needs).
- Multi-variant routing: route low-latency traffic to FP16 primary; on capacity or cost pressure, fall back to quantized variant in the same region.
- KV cache: per-customer prefix cache with sticky routing to keep cache locality; TTL 24h + warm-up heuristics.
- Batching: adaptive batching with max batch size 32 and latency cap 120ms for interactive routes. Continuous batching for background/ETL workload.

SLO tradeoffs and knobs
- If we prioritize P95 <=150ms, pragmatic batching cap at 16 for interactive endpoints; increase batching for background jobs.
- P99 improvements driven by cache hit rate; initial focus on reducing cold starts and pre-warming top 200 prefixes.
- Quantized fallback reduces cost ~35–50% observed in similar customers, but we need a small eval suite to confirm quality regressions.

Immediate next steps (owners & dates)
- JW (Jordan): send this recap + deck (done) and coordinate a short follow-up to review SLO telemetry (by 2026-08-11).
- KI (Karthik): produce a canary topology and cost delta estimate (quantized vs FP16) and list HW assumptions (by 2026-08-16).
- MC (Marissa): run a microbenchmark for KV cache cold-start & warm-up and share traces (by 2026-08-14).
- Alice / Remotescale: share procurement timeline, compliance checklist, and security contact for pen-test scheduling.

Attachments: remotescale-postcall-slides.pdf (post-call deck), latency-samples.csv (sample traces).

Open questions we want to confirm on the next call
- Which endpoints are latency-critical vs cost-critical? (this affects batching thresholds and routing).
- Are there existing prefix sets you want prioritized for KV cache warming?
- Any contractual constraints on quantized model variants (e.g., licensing)?

Thanks — happy to walk through the topology sketch live. If this aligns, we’ll kick off the canary plan and book a 30-min technical review with your infra team.

— Jordan

Looping in a short plan and one concern.

Plan (KV cache microbenchmark)
- Test harness: replay top-150 prefixes at production QPS for a 1-hour window, measure cold->warm P95/P99 and cache hit curve.
- Env: run on a small reserved pool (2x A100-80GB equiv) to mirror their expected model footprint.
- Deliverable: CSV (P50/P95/P99), raw traces, and a short note on warm-up heuristics. Due 2026-08-14 EOD.

Concern
- Cold-starts are highly sensitive to placement/affinity. If we do sticky routing per customer to preserve cache locality, we need to ensure capacity fragmentation does not increase cost materially. I’ll flag any fragmentation estimates in my write-up.

Attaching a quick sketch of the recommended deployment flow (deployment-sketch.svg) — will include it in the follow-up packet.

— Marissa
